atoms.what_it_does: Declares seven Claude lifecycle hook routes and sends every declared route to the same stern.py hook dispatcher command, with per-event timeouts.
atoms.why_it_exists: Centralizes lifecycle entry into one deterministic control fan-in instead of multiple hook-owned state authorities.
atoms.failure_mode: If dispatcher semantics diverge internally, a single fan-in can still hide per-event failures; configuration alone does not prove runtime firing.
atoms.concurrency_implication: Per-event subprocess fan-in avoids seven separate persistent authorities but may create concurrent dispatcher invocations across sessions.
atoms.latency_or_cost_implication: Hook-level timeout caps are 2-8 seconds depending on lifecycle event.
atoms.state_lifetime: hook invocation scoped; durable effects externalized
known_counterevidence: Source configuration is not independent proof that every host/session type fires every route.
open_questions: Which Triggerword-4 scheduler/caller will replace or preserve each lifecycle edge while keeping one state/effect authority?

atoms.concurrency_implication: Module-global DB_PATH plus long-lived in-process imports require explicit refresh/invalidation semantics when path/config changes.

hypotheses: The most reusable Frankenstein-2.0 donor invariant is not stern.py as one giant file but the single deterministic authority fan-in plus explicit epistemic/effect boundaries; GRID10 should preserve the authority topology while decomposing implementation responsibilities.

The 2026-08-26/27 chronology suggests recurring failures came from source-ready mechanisms not being consumed by the live caller/scheduler, from long-lived in-process stale caches after subprocess elimination, and from telemetry that lost decision margins; these three failure classes should become explicit Triggerword-4 acceptance tests.
The sparse generative world substrate should consume typed evidence and verified outcome refs through GRID-controlled capabilities, never direct arbitrary reads from Voice/executor paths.
counterhypotheses: stern.py centralization may be accidental code concentration rather than the correct future authority boundary; a smaller deterministic control fabric can preserve one authority while splitting source files and processes safely.

Shared voice/visual arbitration may only appear reusable because both current paths were engineered around the same scoring vocabulary; GRID10 may need a typed normalization layer before shared competition rather than reusing the raw formula.

The current live-feed/inbox mismatch may be a temporary branch migration state rather than a semantic conflict; do not retire either path until authority explicitly selects the successor and packet equivalence is checked.
